protections: P1: every filesystem path SSG produces from a route (file to write and directories to create) must remain inside the configured output directory (options.dir, default './static', src/helper/ssg/ssg.ts:21,410). Pinned code has no such check at any SSG site.

traps.reason_to_dismiss: routePath is assembled from the app's own route table plus its ssgParams data at build time (src/helper/ssg/ssg.ts:253,275; src/helper/ssg/middleware.ts:43), and only 200 responses are saved (src/helper/ssg/plugins.ts:13), so a solver can argue the value is trusted build configuration rather than attacker input.

Directory creation reads as a harmless side effect of the write, so a guard wrapped around only the writeFile calls (src/helper/ssg/ssg.ts:318,320) still lets the recursive mkdir (src/helper/ssg/ssg.ts:314) create trees outside outDir, and the module-level createdDirs cache (src/helper/ssg/ssg.ts:298) records that path so the escape is not retried.

saveContentToFile and fetchRoutesContent are marked @experimental low-level APIs, so a solver can guard only the documented toSSG entry point (src/helper/ssg/ssg.ts:357) and treat direct callers of the exported helpers as trusted; both helpers, and the routePath they emit, are however part of the public hono/ssg export (src/helper/ssg/index.ts:6, package.json:268-271).

All four returns of generateFilePath funnel into joinPaths, so one leaf check is assumed to cover every shape; but the early returns compose different strings (extension kept at :53, index.html appended at :60, extension appended at :62), normalizePath first rewrites backslashes to '/' (src/helper/ssg/utils.ts:17), and a lexical prefix comparison is walked around by sibling dirs ('static' vs 'static-evil') while the saved routePath is the pre-normalized string (src/helper/ssg/ssg.ts:275) although the request URL is dot-segment-normalized (src/hono-base.ts:502-507).

Hardening the path join at the shared layer looks like the tidy fix and appears not to touch normal output; but joinPaths is contractually documented to resolve '..' above its first argument (src/helper/ssg/utils.test.ts:11,16,21,22) and must keep producing dot-bearing names such as '.test..' (utils.test.ts:23) and '/bravo/deep.dive.to.html' (ssg.test.tsx:393), while './static' must still normalize to 'static/...' (ssg.test.tsx:423) and the directory may come from the default (src/helper/ssg/ssg.ts:21,410).

conflicts.what: A lexical prefix containment check at the sink conflicts with existing normalization: './static' is expected to become 'static/...' (src/helper/ssg/ssg.test.tsx:423), while a prefix test without a separator lets a sibling dir sharing the prefix through, and a substring '..' test rejects legitimate dot-bearing names.

The shared-layer fix for T1, clamping joinPaths so it cannot rise above its base (src/helper/ssg/utils.ts:50-55), contradicts that helper's tested contract that '..' resolves above its first argument (src/helper/ssg/utils.test.ts:11,16,21,22) and breaks the dot-bearing names in T5; the containment check must live at the SSG sink instead.

fairness_risks: joinPaths is documented by tests to resolve '..' upward (src/helper/ssg/utils.test.ts:11,16,21,22); a rule that forbids any resolution above the base breaks that contract and the helper's other users.

Legitimate output names contain dots and even '..' inside a segment: '.test..' and '...' (src/helper/ssg/utils.test.ts:18,23), '/bravo/deep.dive.to.html' and '/bravo/2024.02.18-sweet-memories' and '/bravo/index.tar.gz' (src/helper/ssg/ssg.test.tsx:386-398); a substring or split-on-dot rejection refuses them.

routePath legitimately ends with the output extension ('/index.html', src/helper/ssg/ssg.test.tsx:383,424) and with a trailing slash ('/bravo.text/', src/helper/ssg/ssg.test.tsx:395-396,444); rejecting those shapes as suspicious would break the documented SSG behaviour.

The output directory is a free-form option and defaults to './static' (src/helper/ssg/ssg.ts:21,410); a containment rule relative to process.cwd(), or a comparison against options.dir verbatim instead of its normalized form, contradicts existing output paths (src/helper/ssg/ssg.test.tsx:423).
Recursive creation of nested directories under outDir must keep working and is cached per dir (src/helper/ssg/ssg.ts:298,313-315; src/helper/ssg/ssg.test.tsx:457-468).

design.why: All five candidate sites are closed by one guard placed in saveContentToFile before the mkdir at src/helper/ssg/ssg.ts:311-315 (or equivalently inside generateFilePath, since it has no other caller), so they form a single independent group and cannot supply the 3-5 independent traps a stacked task needs. The best available task is a single-guard fix whose difficulty comes only from the check shape (T4: branch composition, backslash normalization, lexical-vs-resolved and sibling-prefix) and from preserving coupled values (T5), with the DeepSeek-style dismissal being that the traversal value is build-time configuration (T1). Adding T2/T3 as separate traps would double-count the same guard.

No containment check exists anywhere under src/helper/ssg (generateFilePath ssg.ts:44-63, saveContentToFile ssg.ts:299-323, joinPaths utils.ts:50-55), and ssg.test.tsx contains no traversal regression test, so whether A's fix leaves B open cannot be judged from this checkout; the pin appears to predate or omit the A fix.
B-fix content (3a67f7f3997e) and which function it changes (joinPaths, generateFilePath, or saveContentToFile) is not observable from the pinned tree.

The advisory's attacker-input path is not documented in-repo. Reaching a write requires a 200 response for the URL-normalized request (src/hono-base.ts:502-507 strips dot segments; the saved routePath at src/helper/ssg/ssg.ts:275 stays lexical), so a catch-all or wildcard route answering 200 is needed; that combination is inferred, not evidenced by a test.
The Bun adapter's no-op mkdir (src/adapter/bun/ssg.ts:17) differs from the Deno module (src/adapter/deno/ssg.ts:15-17); it looks functional rather than security-related and is not counted as a trap.

extensionMap from options is developer configuration and determineExtension returns its value verbatim (src/helper/ssg/ssg.ts:88-96); a crafted map value could shape the extension, but no attacker-controlled producer of that option exists in-repo, so it is not recorded as a trap.

The repo contains an older lexical '..' rejection in src/utils/filepath.ts:38-40 used by serve-static; the pinned SSG code does not call it, but whether it was added by the A fix is not determinable from the tree.
